items.t: Live data, not pictures of data
items.p: Earthquakes, storms, lightning, satellites and the Moon update while you teach, straight from USGS, NOAA, NASA, EUMETSAT and others.

items.t: Every number has its source, and its blind spot
items.p: Each figure links to the agency that measured it, with what that measurement can't show. Students learn to read data the way scientists do.
Every mission is told four ways, for ages 6–8, 9–11, 12–14 and 15 and up, on the same live globe. Mixed-age classes and homeschool families can work side by side.

items.t: From the schoolyard to the edge of the universe
items.p: One continuous zoom: Earth, the Moon, the planets, a million stars measured by ESA's Gaia, 43,000 real galaxies and the oldest light in the universe.

items.t: History in the words of the people it happened to
items.p: Untold history puts primary sources first: the voices of those it happened to, beside the official account and what is still disputed.

items.t: Worksheets that change with the news
items.p: Print a worksheet and answer key for any mission; its live questions are built from that day's data, so no two weeks are the same.
No accounts, no ads, no cookies, nothing about students stored or sold. Progress stays in each browser.
The code is public (AGPL) and the data policy explains how every layer is made, so you can check our work.
